{{Short description|American football player (1968–2021)}} {{for|the American football quarterback|Keithen McCant}} {{Use American English|date=September 2021}} {{Use mdy dates|date=March 2024}} {{Infobox NFL biography | name = Keith McCants | number = 52, 78, 90 | position = [[Linebacker]]
[[Defensive end]] | birth_date = {{birth date|1968|4|19}} | birth_place = [[Mobile, Alabama]], U.S. | death_date = {{death date and age|2021|9|2|1968|4|19}} | death_place = [[St. Petersburg, Florida]], U.S. | height_ft = 6 | height_in = 3 | weight_lb = 260 | high_school = [[Murphy High School (Alabama)|Murphy]] (Mobile) | college = [[Alabama Crimson Tide football|Alabama]] | draftyear = 1990 | draftround = 1 | draftpick = 4 | pastteams = * [[Tampa Bay Buccaneers]] ({{NFL Year|1990|1992}}) * [[New England Patriots]] (1993)* * [[Houston Oilers]] ({{NFL Year|1993|1994}}) * [[Arizona Cardinals]] (1994) * [[St. Louis Rams]] (1995)* * Arizona Cardinals ({{NFL Year|1995}}) | highlights = * [[Unanimous All-American]] ([[1989 College Football All-America Team|1989]]) * First-team [[List of All-SEC football teams|All-SEC]] ([[1989 All-SEC football team|1989]]) * [[CBS]] National Defensive Player of the Year (1989) * [[Iron Bowl]] MVP (1989) * [[1988 Sun Bowl]] champion | statlabel1 = [[Tackle (football move)|Tackle]]s | statvalue1 = 192 | statlabel2 = [[Quarterback sack|Sack]]s | statvalue2 = 13.5 | statlabel3 = [[Touchdown]]s | statvalue3 = 2 | pfr = M/McCaKe21 }} '''Alvin Keith McCants''' (April 19, 1968 – September 2, 2021) was an American professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[linebacker]] for six seasons in the [[National Football League]] (NFL) for the [[Tampa Bay Buccaneers]], the [[Houston Oilers]], and the [[Arizona Cardinals]] from 1990 to 1995. He played [[college football]] for the [[Alabama Crimson Tide football|Alabama Crimson Tide]], earning [[unanimous All-American]] honors in 1989. He was selected by Tampa Bay in the first round of the [[1990 NFL draft]] with the fourth overall pick. After his playing career, he became a radio broadcaster. ==Early life== McCants attended [[Murphy High School (Alabama)|Murphy High School]] in Mobile, Alabama. As a senior, he amassed 130 tackles and 3 interceptions and was named to the 1986 1st Team All State Team. Additionally, McCants was named to the 1986 Alabama Sports Writers Association's Super 12 team, composed of the top 12 high school football players in the state.{{Cite web |title=Ed King |url=https://www.ahsfhs.org/legends/playersbio1c.asp?id=2925 |access-date=2025-04-04 |website=Alabama High School Football}} McCants was also on the school's basketball team, and helped lead them to the state tournament both his freshman and senior year.{{Cite news |last=Lowry |first=Bruce |date=1987-03-06 |title=Future Tiders lookin' good |url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?id=gTodAAAAIBAJ&sjid=7aUEAAAAIBAJ&pg=6185,2396759&dq=keith+mccants&hl=en |access-date=2025-04-04 |website=The Tuscaloosa News |pages=17 |via=Google News Archive}} ==College career== A college standout at the [[University of Alabama]], McCants had a number of accolades bestowed upon him including being named a 1989 Unanimous First-team [[All-American]] (AP, UPI, WCFF,{{Cite web |title=All-America Teams |url=http://waltercamp.org/index.php/teams_and_awards/ |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090330065940/http://waltercamp.org/index.php/teams_and_awards |archive-date=March 30, 2009 |website=Walter Camp Football Foundation}} AFCA, FWAA, FN, TSN) and a 1989 [[Butkus Award]] Runner-up.{{Cite web |title=Keith McCants, Alabama Crimson Tide, Football |url=http://www.lostlettermen.com/keith_mccants-alabama-football-sec-p128671 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110427135553/http://www.lostlettermen.com/keith_mccants-alabama-football-sec-p128671 |archive-date=2011-04-27 |website=LostLettermen.com}} He was a member of the [[1990 Sugar Bowl]] team and was named the National Defensive Player of the Year in 1989 by CBS.{{cite web |date=1989-12-02 |title=December 2, 1989 At Auburn, Alabama (CBS-TV) (85,214) |url=http://www.rolltide.com/archive_files/files/football/1989/GameRecaps/89recapAU.pdf |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120717081037/http://www.rolltide.com/archive_files/files/football/1989/GameRecaps/89recapAU.pdf |archive-date=July 17, 2012 |website=Alabama Athletics}} In 1988 as a sophomore, McCants finished second on the team with 78 tackles, second only to [[Derrick Thomas]]. Additionally, McCants recorded the most tackles on the team four times during the 1988 regular season, against Tennessee (8), Mississippi State (14), Auburn (17), and Texas A&M (11).[http://www.rolltide.com/archive_files/files/football/1988/Statistics/88stats.pdf] {{dead link|date=October 2014}}{{cite web |title=1988 Game Recaps |url=http://www.rolltide.com/archive_files/files/football/1988/GameRecaps/88recaps.pdf |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120326074943/http://www.rolltide.com/archive_files/files/football/1988/GameRecaps/88recaps.pdf |archive-date=March 26, 2012 |website=Alamana Athletics}} The Texas A&M game, dubbed the [[Hurricane Bowl]], was originally to take place September 17, but Alabama head coach [[Bill Curry]] refused to travel to College Station due to the threat posed by [[Hurricane Gilbert]].{{Cite news |date=1988-12-02 |title=Alabama romps in 'Hurricane Bowl' |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/tri-city-herald-alabama-romps-in-hurric/169539997/ |access-date=2025-04-04 |work=Tri-City Herald |page=13 |via=[[Newspapers.com]] |agency=Associated Press}} The Tide ended the season with a win against Army in the [[1988 Sun Bowl]], in which McCants had a game-high 13 tackles.{{Cite news |date=1988-12-26 |title=Late drive has stars singing the Blues |url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?id=I9xHAAAAIBAJ&sjid=pP8MAAAAIBAJ&pg=1939,7041580&dq=keith+mccants+award&hl=en |access-date=2025-04-04 |website=Record-Journal |pages=16 |via=Google News Archive |agency=Associated Press}} In 1989, he led the Crimson Tide with 119 tackles and 4 sacks. After Alabama's victory against Tennessee, McCants was named the SEC Defensive Player of the Week by the league office{{Cite news |date=1989-10-24 |title=Alabama players chosen for awards |url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?id=RGgfAAAAIBAJ&sjid=59QEAAAAIBAJ&pg=4315,2736854&dq=keith+mccants+award&hl=en |access-date=2025-04-04 |website=Gadsden Times |page=D3 |via=Google News Archive}} for his 16 tackles and two sacks. Three weeks later, he was named ''[[Sports Illustrated]]'' defensive player of the week after totaling 18 tackles in an Alabama victory over [[LSU]]. In the last game of the 1989 regular season against [[Auburn University|Auburn]], dubbed the [[Iron Bowl]], McCants was named the CBS Player of the Game for Alabama with 18 tackles, an interception, and a forced fumble. A high point for the Tide from the game was McCants' display of "incredible athletic talent" in running down Auburn receiver Shane Wasden from behind and preventing a touchdown. Additionally, it was the second straight Iron Bowl in which McCants led the Tide in tackles, combining for 35 total between the 1988 and 1989 matchups. Even with the loss to Auburn, Alabama would still claim the title of 1989 SEC Champions, the school’s first conference title since 1981. Among a number of individual honors, McCants finished his college career with 197 total tackles, including 16 tackles for a loss.{{cite web |title=The Record Book |url=http://grfx.cstv.com/photos/schools/alab/sports/m-footbl/auto_pdf/history-stats.pdf |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090320130713/http://grfx.cstv.com/photos/schools/alab/sports/m-footbl/auto_pdf/history-stats.pdf |archive-date=March 20, 2009 |website=The University Of Alabama}} Additionally, McCants 119 tackles that year puts him tied for 6th all time for tackles in a single season by an Alabama player.{{cite web |date=2004-10-09 |title=Alabama Football Game notes: Oct. 9, 2004 |url=http://www.rolltide.com/archive_files/files/football/2004/gamenotes/bama_kentucky.pdf |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120616210523/http://www.rolltide.com/archive_files/files/football/2004/gamenotes/bama_kentucky.pdf |archive-date=June 16, 2012 |website=Alabama Crimson Tide}} The February 12, 1990, issue of ''Sports Illustrated'' ran an article that focused on McCants titled "The Young and the Restless", that profiled his and other college juniors' eventually successful attempts to declare for the NFL Draft before their senior season, a then-uncommon practice.{{cite news |date=1990-02-12 |title=The Young And The Restless |url=http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/vault/article/magazine/MAG1069350/1/index.htm |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121104031757/http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/vault/article/magazine/MAG1069350/1/index.htm |archive-date=November 4, 2012 |work=Sports Illustrated}}{{Cite web|url=https://exploreuk.uky.edu/cgi/t/text/pageviewer-idx?c=ukmbbprog;cc=ukmbbprog;q1=keith+mccants;rgn=full+text;idno=ukawcp1989_14_21;didno=ukawcp1989_14_21;view=pdf;seq=17;passterms=1|title=ExploreUK - rare and unique research materials from UK Libraries.|website=exploreuk.uky.edu}} In December 2010, [[Bleacher Report]] named McCants the 33rd greatest player in Alabama Crimson Tide History.{{Cite web|url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/536070-the-50-greatest-players-in-alabama-crimson-tide-football-history|title=The 50 Greatest Players In Alabama Crimson Tide Football History|first=Michael|last=Pinto|website=Bleacher Report}} Before the draft, Ed Sherman of the [[Chicago Tribune]] described McCants as "the biggest star around", with pro scouts "drooling over him", and projected him to be "a virtual lock to be the top pick in next spring`s NFL draft". [https://www.chicagotribune.com/1989/12/28/bama-star-weighs-the-pros-cons/ `BAMA STAR WEIGHS THE PROS, CONS] ==Professional career== McCants was for a time expected to be the first player selected in the [[1990 NFL draft]], but the [[Atlanta Falcons]] backed off due to rumors of knee trouble and allegations that his family had been paid money by a sports agent while he was still in college.Associated Press. "Falcons sour on McCants, want George with top pick". The Gadsden Times. April 11, 1990. Still, McCants' strength and 4.51 second time in the [[40-yard dash]]{{Cite news |date=1989-12-06 |title=Ware, Thompson top names on All-American unit |url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?id=dX0_AAAAIBAJ&sjid=MFUMAAAAIBAJ&pg=6823,4802218&dq=keith+mccants+record&hl=en |access-date=2025-04-04 |website=Portsmouth Daily Times |pages=16 |via=Google News Archive |agency=Associated Press}} guaranteed he would still be a high pick, if not #1. After being drafted fourth overall by the Buccaneers in 1990,{{Cite web |title=1990 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/1990/draft.htm |access-date=May 24, 2023 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}} McCants signed a 5-year, $7.4 million deal with the team, including a then-record $2.5 million cash signing bonus.{{Cite news |date=1990-07-12 |title=McCants' deal includes record bonus |url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?id=4KxdAAAAIBAJ&sjid=jV0NAAAAIBAJ&pg=3353,1712387&dq=keith+mccants+named&hl=en |access-date=2025-04-04 |website=Observer-Reporter |page=B6 |via=Google News Archive |agency=Associated Press}}{{cite news |date=July 11, 1990 |title=Buccaneers Sign Keith McCants for $7.4 Million |url=https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-1990-07-11-sp-416-story.html |url-access=subscription |access-date=2025-04-04 |work=Los Angeles Times |agency=Associated Press}} A highly touted prospect, McCants rookie card by [[Score Entertainment|Score]] quoted former Kentucky head coach [[Jerry Claiborne]] as saying "Keith is one of the best football players I have ever seen. Have you ever seen a linebacker as big as he is? I never have. He looks like an elephant and he runs like a deer". Buccaneers coach [[Ray Perkins (wide receiver)|Ray Perkins]] said that "He plays like he is never out of the play. That is an intensity level I like".{{Cite news |last=Pino |first=Mark |date=1990-07-13 |title=McCants signs, gets serious about football |work=The Ocala Star-Banner}} [[Floyd Peters]] was brought to the Bucs in 1991, and converted McCants from a linebacker to [[defensive end]]. Although McCants resisted the change, Peters convinced him that with time he could become a success story along the lines of [[Chris Doleman]], another Peters conversion.{{cite news |last=Zier |first=Patrick |date=1992-08-19 |title=Bucs' McCants would rather be linebacker |url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?id=fMAfAAAAIBAJ&pg=1280,2417157&dq=keith+mccants&hl=en |access-date=2025-04-04 |work=Gadsden Times |page=D4 |via=Google News Archive}} Although privately unhappy he accepted the position, and tried to make the best of it, claiming "Teams won't take me lightly. I can tell you that...I can play any position on this football team, except maybe quarterback. When this season is over, I could be in the Pro Bowl. You don't know how hungry I am. It doesn't matter what position I'm playing. What matters is me."{{Cite web |date=1991-07-24 |title=McCant's Trying New Line Of Work |url=https://www.orlandosentinel.com/1991/07/24/mccants-trying-new-line-of-work/ |access-date=2025-04-04 |website=Orlando Sentinel |language=en-US}} Although McCants was not fond of the move, he did have some success, as he led the Buccaneers in 1991 with 34 quarterback pressures and recorded 5 sacks, prompting Patrick Zier of the ''New York Times'' to remark "considering the circumstances, McCants first year was a success. . .despite having to learn an entirely new position". In December 1991, Coach Peters told the media "I think he's played a decent season. If you watch films, Keith is a producer."{{Cite web |date=1991-12-06 |title=McCants' Unhappy At End |url=https://www.orlandosentinel.com/1991/12/06/mccants-unhappy-at-end/ |access-date=2025-04-04 |website=Orlando Sentinel |language=en-US}} McCants continued to build upon his experience and was second on the Buccaneers in sacks (5) and quarterback pressures (21) in 1992. Eventually, Tampa Bay cut him during their 1993 [[National Football League Training Camp|training camp]]. Within 48 hours, he was picked up off waivers by the [[New England Patriots]], where he was reunited once again with [[Ray Perkins]], then New England's [[Offensive coordinator]].{{Cite news |date=1993-08-27 |title=Patriots trade Vaughn, pick up Keith McCants |url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?id=5_ghAAAAIBAJ&sjid=taIFAAAAIBAJ&pg=1428%2C5145276 |access-date=2025-04-04 |work=Reading Eagle |page=C3 |via=Google News Archive}} Regarding his cut from the Bucs and resigning, McCants remarked at the time "This is a lot off my shoulders...The rumors had been spreading for some time now concerning my future with Tampa."{{Cite web |date=1993-08-27 |title=Patriots Pick Up Ex-Buc McCants |url=https://www.orlandosentinel.com/1993/08/27/patriots-pick-up-ex-buc-mccants/ |access-date=2025-04-04 |website=Orlando Sentinel |language=en-US}} He played in a preseason game the day he was signed, against the [[Kansas City Chiefs]], before being released. In 1993 while with the Houston Oilers, McCants stepped in to separate [[Buddy Ryan]] and [[Kevin Gilbride]] when Ryan punched Gilbride in the face following an Oilers fumble.{{YouTube|bPK3cDl7Ftw|Buddy Ryan punching Kevin Gilbride}} That season, the Oilers would go on to finish first in the [[AFC Central]] Division, sending them to their seventh straight postseason, and McCants's first. When asked what it meant to go to the playoffs, McCants replied, "Let me tell you something, this is big-time. This is football ... I haven't had a winning season since I left college, and it feels great to win again."{{cite news |last=Banks |first=Don |date=December 22, 1993 |title=McCants' move: castoff to playoffs |url=https://www.tampabay.com/archive/1993/12/22/mccants-move-castoff-to-playoffs/ |access-date=2025-04-04 |work=St. Petersburg Times}} In 1994, McCants went to the Cardinals, following Buddy Ryan to Arizona after he was named head coach. In a game against the [[Chicago Bears]], McCants picked off [[Steve Walsh (American football)|Steve Walsh]] and ran back a 46-yard touchdown; it was the Cardinals' longest interception return of the season.{{Cite web|url=http://www.nfl.com/teams/arizonacardinals/statistics?season=1994&team=ARI&seasonType=|title=Arizona Cardinals Stats at NFL.com|website=[[NFL.com]] }} In 1995 McCants scored his second NFL touchdown, on a fumble recovery against the [[Seattle Seahawks]]. ===NFL statistics=== {| class="wikitable" |- ! This was his first full-time role as a broadcaster. He interviewed guests [[Cornelius Bennett]],{{Cite web |date=September 21, 2019 |title=Keith McCants Interviews Cornelius Bennett 9/20/19 |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=NrM382ShcJQ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/varchive/youtube/20211215/NrM382ShcJQ |archive-date=December 15, 2021 |via=YouTube}}{{cbignore}} [[Robert Jones (linebacker)|Robert Jones]], [[Stylez G. White]], [[George Teague]],{{Cite web |date=October 22, 2019 |title=Keith McCants Interviews George Teague on 820 AM |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=5_BXLSBIsOM |url-status=live |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/varchive/youtube/20211215/5_BXLSBIsOM |archive-date=December 15, 2021 |via=YouTube}}{{cbignore}} [[Willie Anderson (offensive tackle)|Willie Anderson]],{{Cite web |date=October 21, 2019 |title=Keith McCants Interviews Willie Anderson |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=y4Q59e-K0cw |url-status=live |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/varchive/youtube/20211215/y4Q59e-K0cw |archive-date=December 15, 2021 |via=YouTube}}{{cbignore}} [[Kato Kaelin]] and [[Ron Jeremy]]. ==Personal life== McCants and [[Emmitt Smith]] became friends while both playing in the SEC in college, with both being named to the 1989 All American team. Smith twice called McCants for advice leading up to his decision to announce for the 1990 Draft.{{Cite news |last=Manuel |first=Marlon |date=1990-02-01 |title=Smith leaving Florida for NFL |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-atlanta-constitution-smith-leaving-f/169540450/ |access-date=2025-04-04 |work=The Atlanta Journal-Constitution |page=F3 |via=[[Newspapers.com]]}} According to his biography, while still a child [[WNBA]] player [[Lindsey Harding]] was inspired by a footrace with McCants to enter the world of sports.{{Cite web |title=Lindsey Harding |url=http://www.actorspages.org/marsharandolph/bio.php?page=bio |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160119190148/http://www.actorspages.org/marsharandolph/bio.php?page=bio |archive-date=January 19, 2016 |website=ActorsPage}} After leaving the NFL, McCants, who studied Criminal Justice while at the University of Alabama, became the first black marine [[police officer]] in the state of Alabama. Working for the Department of Conservation and Natural resources, Conservation Commissioner Riley Boykin Smith said at the time that "he hopes McCants will become the first of many minorities who take advantage of the opportunities to work for his department".{{cite news |date=2000-09-13 |title=Financial setbacks lead McCants to new career |url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?nid=1817&dat=20000913&id=JyMfAAAAIBAJ&pg=2842,2662348 |access-date=October 11, 2014 |work=The Tuscaloosa News |page=3C |via=Google News Archive |agency=Associated Press}}{{cite news |date=2000-09-12 |title=Sports People |url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?nid=1346&dat=20000912&id=wZ4sAAAAIBAJ&pg=6495,414574 |access-date=October 11, 2014 |work=Lakeland Ledger |page=C2 |via=Google News Archive}} McCants was also an avid scuba diver, having dived all around the coast of Florida and the [[Caribbean]]. McCants died of an apparent drug overdose on September 2, 2021, aged 53.{{cite web |last=Heim |first=Mark |date=September 2, 2021 |title=Keith McCants, former NFL and Alabama star, dead at 53 |url=https://www.al.com/alabamafootball/2021/09/keith-mccants-former-nfl-and-alabama-star-dead-at-53.html |access-date=September 2, 2021 |website=AL.com}} ==Media appearances== McCants appeared in the 2012 episode ''Broke'', part of [[ESPN]]'s ''[[30 for 30]]'' series of sports documentaries. The premiere of ''Broke'', which detailed the high rates of [[bankruptcy]] and [[Personal finances of professional American athletes|financial trouble amongst professional athletes]], attracted 2.7 million viewers, an all-time ESPN record.{{cite web |title='Broke' Ranks as ESPN's Highest-Rated '30 for 30' Documentary - Ratings |url=http://tvbythenumbers.zap2it.com/2012/10/04/broke-ranks-as-espns-highest-rated-30-for-30-documentary/151637/ |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141109002014/http://tvbythenumbers.zap2it.com/2012/10/04/broke-ranks-as-espns-highest-rated-30-for-30-documentary/151637/ |archive-date=November 9, 2014 |work=TVbytheNumbers}} McCants was a semi-frequent guest on [[HuffPost Live]], having appeared on the program five times.{{cite news |title=Post-NFL Poverty |url=http://live.huffingtonpost.com/r/segment/is-playing-in-the-nfl/505a3ea82b8c2a743200054b |archive-url=https://archive.today/20130411024535/http://live.huffingtonpost.com/r/segment/is-playing-in-the-nfl/505a3ea82b8c2a743200054b |archive-date=2013-04-11 |work=HuffPost Live}}{{cite news |title=Ban The Kickoff! |url=http://live.huffingtonpost.com/r/segment/football-nfl-kickoffs/50c60cf22b8c2a300f00005d |archive-url=https://archive.today/20130411024955/http://live.huffingtonpost.com/r/segment/football-nfl-kickoffs/50c60cf22b8c2a300f00005d |archive-date=2013-04-11 |work=HuffPost Live}}{{cite news |title=Hazards Of The NFL Trade |url=http://live.huffingtonpost.com/r/segment/nfl-suicide-cte/50bcbc2dfe3444541a00031f |archive-url=https://archive.today/20130411025944/http://live.huffingtonpost.com/r/segment/nfl-suicide-cte/50bcbc2dfe3444541a00031f |archive-date=2013-04-11 |work=HuffPost Live}}{{cite news |title=Sports & Mental Illness |url=http://live.huffingtonpost.com/r/segment/room-for-the-mentally-ill-in-pro-sports%3F/5140fcb62b8c2a0bac00027f |archive-url=https://archive.today/20130411024138/http://live.huffingtonpost.com/r/segment/room-for-the-mentally-ill-in-pro-sports%3F/5140fcb62b8c2a0bac00027f |archive-date=2013-04-11 |work=HuffPost Live}}{{cite news |date=2013-07-25 |title=Former NFL Star: Football Is No Different From Dogfighting |url=http://live.huffingtonpost.com/r/archive/segment/former-nfl-star-football-is-no-different-from-dogfighting/51f187aa78c90a3eeb000428 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20130813013808/http://live.huffingtonpost.com/r/archive/segment/former-nfl-star-football-is-no-different-from-dogfighting/51f187aa78c90a3eeb000428 |archive-date=2013-08-13 |work=HuffPost Live}} Three of the appearances were with host [[Marc Lamont Hill]]. McCants was the guest for the September 21, 2012, episode of ''[[Highly Questionable|Dan Lebatard is Highly Questionable]]''.{{YouTube|L4WEv7RrGUQ}} On September 24, 2012, he appeared as a guest on Kaelin]]'s sports-themed television talk show He also appeared on [[WALA-TV]] Fox 10 a number of times, with segments including "The Interview"{{YouTube|fEagRQwBc04}} and "Studio 10".{{cite web
